The paper was published in Nano-Micro Letters in 2025 (September 15, 2025)
The research was conducted at the State Key Laboratory of Space Power-Sources, School of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Harbin Institute of Technology
Egg white was selected as the protein source for the first time in this type of research
The minimum reflection loss achieved is -72.0 dB, which is superior to many previously reported biomass-derived composites
The effective absorption bandwidth is 6.3 GHz when electromagnetic waves propagate parallel to directional pores
Ammonium metatungstate (AM) acts as both the tungsten source and the salting-out agent
Four samples were prepared with AM dosages of 0.12 g, 0.24 g, 0.36 g, and 0.48 g, designated as WCC-1, WCC-2, WCC-3, and WCC-4
The optimal sample (WCC-2) uses 0.24 g of AM dosage
Pyrolysis occurs in two stages: 450°C for 0.5 hours followed by 800°C for 3 hours
The heating rate from room temperature to 450°C is 3.0°C/min
The heating rate from 450°C to 800°C is 5.0°C/min
Macropore size ranges from 1.0 to 7.0 micrometers in the final foam
Carbon flake thickness is approximately 150 nanometers
WC₁₋ₓ nanoparticle sizes range from 4.0 nm to 14.0 nm depending on AM dosage
The lattice fringe spacing of WC₁₋ₓ nanoparticles is 0.24 nm, corresponding to the (111) plane
Graphitic domains have a lattice fringe spacing of 0.34 nm
The carbon frameworks are amorphous overall at the 800°C pyrolysis temperature
XRD analysis shows characteristic diffraction peaks at 2θ values of 37.2°, 43.1°, 62.2°, and 74.3°
The XRD pattern matches PDF#20–1316 for face-centered cubic tungsten carbide
Nitrogen atoms from egg white are retained in the final carbon framework
The salting-out process causes protein vesicles to form initially, then collapse into protein flakes
Magnetic stirring at 300 rpm for 3 hours is used during the salting-out process
Protein denaturation is ensured by heating at 90°C for 10 minutes
Freeze-drying is performed for 72 hours to prepare the precursor
COMSOL simulation confirms good electromagnetic interference prevention among electronic components
Radar cross section simulation demonstrates considerable reduction with changing incident angles
The tungsten carbide formation temperature (700-900°C) is significantly lower than other carbides like SiC (>1400°C)
The method eliminates the need for specialized unidirectional freezing equipment
Egg white is a waste product from food processing industries, making this approach sustainable
The electrostatic interaction between ammonium metatungstate and protein ensures well-dispersed WC₁₋ₓ nanoparticles
